---
title: "Units of assignment"
execute:
  cache: false
---

The ManyBabies Consortium tested infants' preference for infant-directed speech (IDS) over adult-directed speech (ADS) in a shared multi-laboratory experiment. The primary report describes the stimuli, protocol, exclusions, and analyses ([The ManyBabies Consortium 2020](https://doi.org/10.1177/2515245919900809)); the prepared trial table comes from the [version of the official analysis repository used here](https://github.com/manybabies/mb1-analysis-public/tree/dc3eb5b3578057096d337203635c0759d2fc04b6). We begin with all possible trial rows for the represented infants so that the original assignment and repetition structure remains visible.

```{r}
manybabies <- readRDS("data/manybabies/manybabies1-trials.rds")

stopifnot(
  nrow(manybabies) == 37264L,
  length(unique(manybabies$infant_id)) == 2329L,
  length(unique(manybabies$lab_id)) == 67L,
  all(table(manybabies$infant_id) == 16L),
  all(is.na(manybabies$looking_time_seconds) == manybabies$trial_missing)
)
```

Each infant could encounter sixteen 18-second test stimuli: eight IDS stimuli and eight ADS stimuli. The official exclusion code then completed every retained infant's record to sixteen possible test-trial rows. A row may thus contain an included looking time, recorded trial metadata without an included looking time, or a completed measurement opportunity without recorded trial metadata. No missing looking time has been imputed.

Here **looking time** is the recorded duration, in seconds, for which an infant attended during a test trial under the laboratory's measurement procedure. A possible-trial timeline is: assign the infant one order, present the order's register--stimulus combination at that position, record trial metadata, and retain a looking-time outcome only if the release's inclusion rules are met. The [linguistic-data chapter](../foundations/linguistic-data.qmd#unit-and-observation-key) called this the distinction between a row key and the scientific unit represented through it.

We first map possible rows to infants, laboratories, and recurring stimuli, then measure the unequal information those maps create, and finally state which design claims the release can support.

## Assignment and measurement are different maps

The [**unit of assignment**](https://openstax.org/books/introductory-statistics-2e/pages/1-4-experimental-design-and-ethics), also called the experimental unit, is the smallest entity that can independently receive a condition under the actual procedure. Let $r$ index possible trial rows and let $g(r)$ map row $r$ to its infant. If $Z_i$ is infant $i$'s assigned trial order, then

$$
Z_r=Z_{g(r)}.
$$

All sixteen possible rows from one infant share one order assignment. Under the [definition of independence](../foundations/independence.qmd), separate row identifiers do not create independent assignments when the rows inherit the same random order label.

Other maps are needed as well. Let $l(r)$ identify the laboratory, $p(r)$ the paired stimulus when its metadata were recorded, and $R_r$ indicate whether an included looking time is present. The recorded outcome is then available only when $R_r=1$. These maps keep five roles apart:

1. a possible trial row is a measurement opportunity;
2. an infant is the sampling unit and the order-assignment unit;
3. a laboratory is a cluster within which infants were recruited and tested;
4. a paired stimulus recurs across infants;
5. a nonmissing looking time is an observed outcome.

The distinction is empirical in this release. The following code reconstructs the infant table and every count from the RDS file.

```{r}
#| label: show-manybabies-trial-row
manybabies[which(!manybabies$trial_missing)[1L], c(
  "infant_id", "lab_id", "trial_number", "register", "stimulus_id",
  "looking_time_seconds", "counterbalance_order"
)]
```

The displayed row participates in two maps at once: row $\rightarrow$ infant $\rightarrow$ laboratory and row $\rightarrow$ paired stimulus. The first map identifies repeated measurement and recruitment clustering; the second identifies material reuse.

```{r}
usable_by_infant <- aggregate(
  cbind(
    usable_trials = as.integer(!manybabies$trial_missing),
    metadata_rows = as.integer(manybabies$trial_metadata_observed)
  ) ~ infant_id + lab_id,
  data = manybabies,
  FUN = sum
)

registers_by_infant <- tapply(
  manybabies$register[!manybabies$trial_missing],
  manybabies$infant_id[!manybabies$trial_missing],
  function(x) length(unique(x))
)

usable_by_infant$registers_with_data <- 0L
usable_by_infant$registers_with_data[
  match(names(registers_by_infant), usable_by_infant$infant_id)
] <- as.integer(registers_by_infant)

unit_counts <- data.frame(
  unit = c(
    "possible trial rows",
    "rows with recorded trial metadata",
    "rows with included looking time",
    "included infant identifiers",
    "infants with an included looking time",
    "infants represented in both registers",
    "laboratories",
    "paired stimulus IDs"
  ),
  count = c(
    nrow(manybabies),
    sum(manybabies$trial_metadata_observed),
    sum(!manybabies$trial_missing),
    length(unique(manybabies$infant_id)),
    sum(usable_by_infant$usable_trials > 0L),
    sum(usable_by_infant$registers_with_data == 2L),
    length(unique(manybabies$lab_id)),
    length(unique(stats::na.omit(manybabies$stimulus_id)))
  )
)

knitr::kable(unit_counts, format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```

The table contains `r format(nrow(manybabies), big.mark = ",")` possible trial rows but only `r format(length(unique(manybabies$infant_id)), big.mark = ",")` infant assignment units. Looking time is included on `r format(sum(!manybabies$trial_missing), big.mark = ",")` rows. And only `r format(sum(usable_by_infant$registers_with_data == 2L), big.mark = ",")` infants can enter the paired IDS-minus-ADS summary developed on the [within-participant page](within-participant-designs.qmd).

## Unequal information within laboratories

Infants are nested within laboratories, but the number of included trials varies across infants. The gray points below are infants; the blue point is the laboratory median. Laboratory labels are suppressed because the figure concerns the dependence structure, not a ranking of sites.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 6.2
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-alt: "Included looking-time trials for every infant, grouped by laboratory, with a median point for each laboratory."

ggplot2::ggplot(
  usable_by_infant,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = stats::reorder(lab_id, usable_trials, FUN = median),
    y = usable_trials
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(
    alpha = 0.22, # dqr-allow: algorithm-setting
    size = 0.75,
    color = "grey25",
    position = ggplot2::position_jitter(width = 0.18, height = 0)
  ) +
  ggplot2::stat_summary(
    fun = median,
    geom = "point",
    color = "#2C6E9B",
    size = 1.6
  ) +
  ggplot2::coord_flip() +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "Laboratory",
    y = "Included looking-time trials per infant"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_classic(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )
```

Additional trials may improve the measurement of a particular infant's looking behavior, and additional infants may improve the comparison across infants. They are not interchangeable. Likewise, eight recurring paired stimuli supply repeated material measurements, not eight additional infant assignments.

## What this release can establish

The final table begins after participant- and laboratory-level exclusions. It can establish the units present in the released analysis table, but it cannot reconstruct the full recruitment process from the retained records alone. This limit is why a design audit should name the unit at each stage rather than infer recruitment from the number of rows.

::: {.callout-note title="Audit the ManyBabies units"}
1. Why do sixteen possible rows for one infant still represent one order assignment?
2. Which map identifies dependence induced by testing infants in the same laboratory?
3. Why do additional trials and additional infants provide different kinds of information?
4. Which infants can enter an infant-weighted IDS-minus-ADS comparison?
:::

<details class="understanding-answers">
<summary>Answers</summary>

1. Order is assigned once to the infant, so all sixteen rows inherit the same $Z_i$.
2. The map $l(r)$ from trial row to laboratory identifies shared testing and recruitment context.
3. More trials refine an infant's response summary, while more infants add assignment and sampling units.
4. Only infants with included IDS and ADS outcomes can supply the paired register contrast.

</details>

The unit of assignment is the smallest entity whose assigned condition could vary independently under the procedure. In ManyBabies 1, order varies between infants, register varies within infants, and looking-time measurements repeat within infants, laboratories, and paired stimuli.

## Recap and forward link

1. A possible trial row is a measurement opportunity, not an independent assignment.
2. The infant is the order-assignment and sampling unit.
3. Laboratory and stimulus maps identify two additional dependence structures.

The next page asks what the public release can and cannot establish about the [assignment mechanism](random-assignment.qmd#the-assignment-mechanism-is-a-probability-rule).
